ParlaMint-AT_2014-05-21-025-XXV-NRSITZ-00027_d8e27609	Mr President. Mr. Minister! Ladies and gentlemen! Dear spectators in front of the screens at home! In Austria, there is currently the only model of collective enforcement of law, the collective action developed by the Judicatur under Austrian law. In doing so, all parties to the proceedings must resign their claims for damages to an association of complainants, such as the Consumer Information Association, which then sues the claims collected from the court. Although this model is quite successful, which underlines the need for such an instrument, in practice it leads to high costs and complex processes. A group action would be significantly more favourable, since the applicants for legal aid can appeal directly to the Court of First Instance with their claims. Minister Hundstorfer also confirmed some time ago that group complaints are much cheaper than collective complaints. Although there is a draft, there has been no sign of implementation for seven years. Let me give you an example so that you can imagine this better: If 200 people suffer from breakthrough on a cruise, it is not necessary to carry out 200 procedures, nor is it necessary to assign all individual complaints to a collection clarifier. In the event of a group complaint, all 200 injured persons may exercise their right in one procedure. We Greens are and have always been for the introduction of the group complaint, but we have been comforted over and over again. Of course, it is also necessary to discuss how many claimants should be able to file such an action. But we are committed to the lowest possible threshold. It would be possible to imagine a circle of 20 to 50 damaged persons. I have already asked Mr Hundstorfer twice whether there will be a group complaint in Austria in the foreseeable future. Twice the answer was short and promising: No, no, no, The Federal Ministry of Labour, Social Affairs and Consumer Protection is financing the Association for Consumer Information in the submission of collective complaints. These costs could be saved when introducing the group complaint. On the one hand, one speaks of savings or budget losses, and on the other hand, one does not save where it is actually necessary. The Chamber of Workers and the VKI are basically for the introduction of a group complaint. It's not understandable to me why there's nothing going on. It is clear that the EIA absolutely does not want the group complaint to be introduced because behind it is the Chamber of Commerce who, of course, fears mass complaints against companies. This fear is unfounded. Other countries such as England, Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland have introduced the model of group action. We do not need to reinvent the wheel, but we only need to imitate the other countries that have already made it and have success in it. [[Congratulation with the greens.]] Why are we still being asked into the waiting room if there are already good experiences and everything is ready? – The longer it takes, the more it costs the affected life and money. Yesterday, it was criticized that the opposition was always more critical and not proposing. However, proposals to reduce the budget will not be fully implemented. If a draft is in the drawer for seven years and is not dealt with, then the criticism is justified. Thank you.

Another point that we did not think was good – it is a proposal – is that a so-called mandate procedure should be introduced in the event of a criminal threat of up to a year, after which a judge could, in the event of a clear trial, without carrying out a trial, take a judgment that will only be delivered. The culprit is not even loaded, not even heard. We consider this to be highly problematic in the rule of law.
